Habermas’s distinction is that “law as medium” is a formal, general-rule steering mechanism that coordinates and controls systemic spheres like the state and economy, while “law as institution” is anchored in the lifeworld’s shared norms, values, and democratic legitimacy. In short, law as medium serves systemic efficiency and control, whereas law as institution serves normative integration and communicative rationality.
